+## Glossary

+*The internal names this document uses, each defined in the programme’s own words with where the programme states it. The block is printed by relay `tools/chain_page.py` from relay `data/glossary.txt`, one source shared by the two generated pages and the keystone census, so it reads the same in all three.*

+- **A PLACE TO STAND** — the research programme whose papers, kernels and ledgers this corpus holds: its principal result "a machine-verified reduction of the Riemann Hypothesis to a single located clause, with that clause carried openly as open" *(OPEN_TRAILS :12354, "the programme is the A PLACE TO STAND research programme"; README :1, :22-:23)*

+- **RH** — the Riemann Hypothesis, as Mathlib states it (`RiemannHypothesis`): every zero s of the Riemann zeta function that is not a trivial zero −2(n+1) and is not s = 1 has real part 1/2 *(Mathlib de5ce8a9, NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean :185)*

+- **GRH_chi** — the same statement for the zeros of the L-function of one primitive Dirichlet character χ ≠ 1; GRH, the generalised Riemann Hypothesis for these characters, is GRH_chi for every such χ *(README :125, the author's ruling (R183)(3))*

+- **the located clause** — the Riemann Hypothesis holds exactly when the explicit-formula quadratic form Q(k) = pole term − prime sum + archimedean term is non-negative for every admissible test window k, the theorem h2_sign_iff_rh deriving the equivalence with no premise, and the open clause being the sign statement h2_sign itself, which the kernel states, proves equivalent to RH, bounds by its mechanism exclusions, and carries as its one open premise *(the author's ruling (R248)(4); README :22-:23, "a machine-verified reduction of the Riemann Hypothesis to a single located clause, with that clause carried openly as open")*
+- **h2** — the programme's name for the open clause; in the kernel it is the one Prop h2_sign *(SIDE-explicit-formula SIDEExplicitFormula/H2Sign.lean :28, "h2, as one Prop")*

+- **h2_sign** — Weil positivity on classK: for every test window k in classK, 0 ≤ P(k) − PR(k) + A(k), the pole term, the prime sum and the archimedean term of the explicit formula; open, and carried as the one open premise *(SIDE-explicit-formula SIDEExplicitFormula/H2Sign.lean :28-:29)*

+- **classK** — the admissible test windows: functions k on the reals that are even, twice continuously differentiable and compactly supported, and of the form h ⋆ h~ with h twice continuously differentiable and compactly supported *(SIDE-explicit-formula SIDEExplicitFormula/H2Sign.lean :22-:26)*

+- **h2_sign_iff_rh** — the compiled theorem h2_sign ↔ RiemannHypothesis: "Weil positivity on classK is Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, both directions, no hypothesis" *(SIDE-explicit-formula SIDEExplicitFormula/Seam.lean :100-:101; README :115)*
+- **Weil positivity** — the statement h2_sign, the non-negativity of the explicit formula's quadratic form on classK, one of three faces of the one open clause compiled as equivalent *(README :121)*
+- **Li positivity** — the non-negativity of Li's coefficients λ_n, compiled over Mathlib's zeros as equivalent to RH (li_nonneg_iff_rh), a second face of the one open clause *(README :121)*

+- **arithmetic-limit positivity** — the non-negativity of the Bombieri–Lagarias arithmetic limits, compiled as equivalent to RH (arith_limit_nonneg_iff_rh), the third face of the one open clause *(README :121)*

+- **seam** — a named implication between open statements, read as a premise when it is the antecedent of a statement's conclusion: rh_strip_imp_rh, that every zero of zeta with real part at most 0 is a trivial zero *(relay tools/e0_rule.py, (R236)(2)(i); README :113)*

+- **kernel** — a Lean 4 repository of the programme's federation, checked by Lean on its own and cited by named theorem at a pinned commit or tag: "Lean kernels under psinary-sketch carry the arms" *(README :18)*

+- **SIDE-** — the prefix of every kernel's name, one public repository each under github.com/psinary-sketch: SIDE-kernel carries the deposited route terminals (v1.5), SIDE-explicit-formula the explicit formula, h2_sign and h2_sign_iff_rh, SIDE-structural-error-correction the error-correction kernel, SIDE-global-section the global-section kernel, and each other SIDE- name the kernel of its own subject *(README :15, :18; SPIRAL_MAP.md, the federation map)*
+- **terminal** — a compiled theorem a paper cites by name: "cited by named terminal, not by count" *(README :15)*
+- **pin** — the commit, or the tag peeling to one, at which a citation is read: "pins move, so the columns are read live, never recalled" *(README :18)*
+- **the standard three** — the axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], written std3 *(README :79-:80)*
+- **Zeta23** — the vendored explicit-formula modules of anthropics/formal-math at 3635e748, on which the explicit-formula kernel builds *(the generated pages' head line)*
+- **Bulka** — the vendored repository nicholasbulka/li-criterion-rh-equivalence-lean at 35df682f under Apache 2.0, the converse half of Li's criterion *(README :121)*

+- **E0** — the shared grading rule, relay tools/e0_rule.py from b568: it grades a theorem by reading its statement's binders, INTERFACES when a hypothesis binder is a named Prop passed through as a premise and DERIVES when its only binders are domain conditions; from b637 every binder is classed by its kind, its typing and its form, its name no part of the reading *(relay tools/e0_rule.py, RULE_TEXT; OPEN_TRAILS :13337)*

+- **binder** — a variable or hypothesis a statement introduces: the header's groups ( ), { }, ⦃ ⦄ and [ ] (Lean's four binder kinds), the conclusion's leading universal telescope, the antecedents of its implication and the binders of an existential in it *(relay data/b637_binder_classes.txt; Lean/Expr.lean :71-:79)*

+- **binder class** — one of the 26 classes B01-B26 the rule reads every binder into, by kind, typing (a Prop or data) and form, each class with its outcome: data, a domain condition, a premise, a seam, an unlisted predicate or part of the conclusion *(relay data/b637_binder_classes.txt; relay tools/e0_rule.py, CLASSES)*

+- **domain condition** — a binder that does not enter the grade: an instance binder whose class is not Fact; a membership, non-membership, non-emptiness or finiteness condition on an object the statement names; a restriction on a variable the same statement quantifies universally *(relay tools/e0_rule.py, (R235)(2))*

+- **premise** — a binder asserting a Prop about a fixed object the kernel names and does not derive: a structure of premises, an EF_lit_* hypothesis, a Fact instance, a Summable or HasSum of the kernel's own series *(relay tools/e0_rule.py, (R235)(2))*
+- **DERIVES** — "the theorem's statement, unfolded to its base objects, establishes the claim" *(README :64-:65)*

+- **INTERFACES** — "the theorem takes the claim as a named hypothesis, discharged elsewhere and identified in the row. This is a legitimate architecture, not a defect; it is how a kernel cites a manuscript result. The row names the premise." *(README :66-:68)*

+- **ENCODES-CONCLUSION** — "the theorem stipulates what the paper claims, or concludes a placeholder. These are work-orders, not citations"; the rule reads it when a hypothesis binder's type is the conclusion itself *(README :69-:71; relay tools/e0_rule.py, (R234)(2))*
+- **SHELL** — read with ENCODES-CONCLUSION: a theorem that concludes a placeholder; a work-order, not a citation *(README :69-:71)*
+- **ENCODES** — the table's synonym for ENCODES-CONCLUSION and ENCODES-CONCLUSION-or-SHELL, applied before ledger cells are compared *(relay tools/terminal_table.py, the synonym map, (R164)(2)(a))*
+- **NOT THE CLAIM** — "the theorem is sound and its statement is strictly weaker than the claim the row makes for it" *(README :72-:73)*
+- **DEF** — the table's grade of a definition: an object or a Prop defined, not a theorem, carrying no claim *(relay data/b637_binder_classes.txt, the grade)*

+- **PREDICATE-UNLISTED** — the rule's reading of a named predicate on a variable the statement quantifies, met for the first time: printed as such and not read as a premise, so the list of named restrictions grows by a ruling and not by a wrong grade *(OPEN_TRAILS :13221)*

+- **MET** — the rule's forward guard: the named predicates any row of the terminal table carried in the rule's reading at relay 8e6b63cc (51 names) and those met since; a name it holds reads as a premise until the author rules it a restriction *(OPEN_TRAILS :13221; relay tools/e0_rule.py, MET)*

+- **CONFLICT** — a row whose ledger cells grade one name differently: "the row records CONFLICT and quotes BOTH WITHOUT CHOOSING -- a table that resolves a disagreement has conferred a grade" *(relay tools/terminal_table.py :10-:12)*
+- **UNGRADED** — a row neither a ledger cell nor the rule grades *(THE_KEYSTONE_CENSUS v0.5 :43, "none (ungraded)")*

+- **the terminal table** — relay data/terminal_table.md and its json: one row per compiled declaration the ledgers or the axiom prints name, each with its grade and the provenance of that grade; "it confers no grade and moves none" *(relay tools/terminal_table.py :1-:12)*

+- **provenance** — where a row's grade comes from: cell (a ledger cell grades it), rule (the shared E0 rule reads its statement), rule-elab (the rule reads the declaration's elaborated type where the textual reading differs or defers) or none (ungraded) *(THE_KEYSTONE_CENSUS v0.5 :43; relay tools/terminal_table.py, (R245)(2)-(3))*

+- **upstream** — the kind of a table row whose declaration lives outside every kernel (Mathlib's, or a vendored module's beyond the kernel's roots): its grade cell reads —, its provenance none, and it is excluded from every grade count; "Mathlib's theorems are cited, not graded" *(OPEN_TRAILS :13335, (R247)(2))*
+- **T0** — the anchor tier: compiled against a Mathlib statement, at the standard three, its statement read *(the author's ruling (R149)(2), relay data/b539_ferry.txt :21-:22)*
+- **T1-open** — compiled in a programme kernel, INTERFACES on a premise equivalent to RH that is named and open; h2_sign is the one open premise of this kind *((R149)(2); FINDINGS :4823, :5812)*
+- **T1-lit** — compiled in a programme kernel, INTERFACES on an uncompiled literature theorem *(FINDINGS :4823, :5812)*
+- **T2** — compiled, but the terminal is ENCODES-CONCLUSION, SHELL, false as stated or vacuous *((R149)(2), relay data/b539_ferry.txt :25-:28)*
+- **T2-INTERFACES** — a terminal that interfaces on a named premise which is neither compiled nor a literature theorem but the programme's own manuscript claim *(FINDINGS :5812, (R165)(3))*
+- **T3** — numerical: VERIFIED-STRICT, -EST or -EST-TAIL, with its bank *((R149)(2), relay data/b539_ferry.txt :28-:29)*
+- **T4** — a reading, manuscript-resident, with no terminal *((R149)(2), relay data/b539_ferry.txt :29-:30)*
+- **keystone** — a document read at Tier K, KC or C under the author-ruled taxonomy: the documents that carry the programme's results to a reader outside it *(THE_KEYSTONE_CENSUS v0.5 :20)*

+- **Tier K, KC, C, N, E** — the author-ruled tiers of a document: Tier K, certification at a pin; Tier KC, certification and cluster synthesis together; Tier C, synthesis; Tier N, notes and exploratory; Tier E, filing-facing *(phase1.5/method/THE_DOCUMENT_CLASS_TAXONOMY.md :14-:20; THE_KEYSTONE_CENSUS v0.5 :20)*

+- **phase** — REGISTRY's divisions of the corpus -- Phase 1 (Day 1), Phase 1.2, Phase 1.5 and Phase 2 -- and within them the lettered clusters (1.5A-1.5H, 2A-2G), each a group of papers on one subject *(REGISTRY.md; THE_KEYSTONE_CENSUS v0.5 :41)*

+- **REGISTRY** — "the single source of truth. One row per paper: ID, title, file, version, confidence mark, status, word count, notes ... If this file disagrees with anything else, it wins" *(README :35)*
+- **FINDINGS** — "the middle reference layer between the kernels ... and the papers, which cite"; append-only *(README :37)*

+- **OPEN_TRAILS** — "the cross-session continuity ledger -- items needing explicit follow-through: open trails, work-orders (W-ORD-*), and research-arc entries with dated addenda"; append-only *(README :36)*
+- **W-ORD** — a work-order on OPEN_TRAILS: a named piece of work, priced and entered, which an act takes up on the author's word *(README :36)*
+- **ERRATA** — "corrections to deposited artifacts, each retained at the version it was filed against" *(README :40)*
+- **SPIRAL_MAP** — "the federation map -- kernels, their relationship to the papers, and the translation table from programme vocabulary to standard mathematics" *(README :39)*
+- **relay** — the programme's working repository (github.com/psinary-sketch/relay): "session reports, computational instruments, and their data banks" *(README :41)*
+- **PLACE-papers** — the corpus's own repository (github.com/psinary-sketch/PLACE-papers): the papers, the registry, the generated pages and the ledgers *(OPEN_TRAILS :12354)*
+- **the sieve** — THE_FINDINGS_AS_THEY_STAND: the sieve table of the programme's findings by cluster, each row with its verdict *(phase2/method/THE_FINDINGS_AS_THEY_STAND_v0_6.md :1)*

+- **the ceiling sentence** — the README's ruled line of what the corpus may claim and what it may not, with each later ruled sentence placed beside it; no document claims beyond it *(README :106, and the ruled sentences beside it, :113-:125)*

+- **Correspondence** — the table that pairs a document's rows with the compiled declarations they cite and grades each pair; with Placement it sits in the back matter *(OPEN_TRAILS :11864, the form of an edition)*
+- **Placement** — the table of where each object a document names lives: its path and its status *(OPEN_TRAILS :11864, the form of an edition)*

+- **the form of an edition** — the standing form by which a document's next version is written beside the current one, the current unedited, its changes recorded in back matter *(OPEN_TRAILS :11864)*
+- **the load-bearing clause** — a kernel-verified terminal counts toward a document's tier only where it carries the thesis of the document's head *(OPEN_TRAILS :12699)*
+- **ANNEX** — REGISTRY's download layer, outside the repository tree and filed non-keystone *(REGISTRY.md :360)*
+- **CP-1** — the first stage of the critical path: the tier blocks appended to each keystone, its terminals tiered T0-T4 *(OPEN_TRAILS :11413)*

+- **bNNN** — an act: one numbered session of the programme's work under the author's ruling (b638 is this one), its banks at relay data/bNNN_*, its record lines in FINDINGS and OPEN_TRAILS *(OPEN_TRAILS :13339, the record of b637)*
+- **(Rnnn)** — the author's rulings, numbered, each ratified by the delivery that carries it and strikeable clause by clause *(the ruling (R248)'s own head)*

+- **the act root** — the sha256 over the repositories' heads, the cited tags and the act's banks, chained to the previous act's root, so that an act's state can be re-read and checked *(relay tools/act_root.py :4-:10; relay data/act_roots.txt)*
+- **the deposit** — a Zenodo record of the programme's work, the author's own act; the Zenodo deposits and the GitHub repositories carry its assertions *(OPEN_TRAILS :12354)*

+- **the mirror** — the project workspace's mirror, a zip of the roster's files: research history at every stage of edit, not definitive where a more refined result supersedes it *(OPEN_TRAILS :12354; relay tools/mirror_roster.json)*
